pharm: A non-colonizing, non-pathogenic yeast that transiently occupies the gut, antagonizes enteric pathogens and their toxins (notably Clostridioides difficile toxins A and B), modulates intestinal immunity and short-chain fatty acid production, and helps restore the gut microbial barrier during and after antibiotic-associated and infectious diarrhea.
quick: 250-500 mg (approx. 5-10 billion CFU) once or twice daily
May be taken with or without food
Generally considered low risk; data limited - use if benefit clear
No specific interaction; alcohol may worsen diarrhea
Symptom response; watch for fungemia in high-risk patients
summary: Saccharomyces boulardii is a probiotic yeast used to prevent and treat diarrheal conditions, including antibiotic-associated diarrhea, Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (as an adjunct), acute infectious diarrhea, and traveler's diarrhea. Being a yeast, it is intrinsically resistant to antibacterial antibiotics and can be co-administered with them. It acts by antagonizing pathogens and their toxins, modulating the immune response, and supporting the intestinal barrier. It is generally well tolerated, but it is contraindicated in critically ill, immunocompromised, or central-venous-catheter patients because of a rare but serious risk of fungemia (Saccharomyces bloodstream infection). It is a supplement/biotherapeutic rather than an FDA-approved drug.
indications: Adjunctive prevention of recurrence of Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea
Treatment of acute infectious (including viral) diarrhea, particularly in children

dosage.d: 250-500 mg (about 5-10 billion CFU) once or twice daily during and shortly after antibiotic course
dosage.n: Can be taken alongside antibiotics (yeast is unaffected by antibacterials)
Dose by product; ensure adequate rehydration

dosage.d: 500 mg twice daily for ~4 weeks alongside standard antibiotic therapy
dosage.n: Adjunct only; not a substitute for C. difficile antibiotics

dosage.d: 250-500 mg daily starting before and during travel

admin: Take by mouth; capsules/sachets may be opened and mixed into cool or lukewarm (not hot) food or drink
Do not mix with very hot liquids, which kill the live yeast
Can be taken at the same time as antibacterial antibiotics (yeast is resistant)
Maintain adequate fluid and electrolyte intake (oral rehydration) during diarrhea
Do NOT open capsules near or handle around immunocompromised patients or central venous catheters (fungemia risk via contamination)
moa: Saccharomyces boulardii is a thermophilic, non-pathogenic yeast that transits the gut without permanently colonizing it. Its beneficial effects are multifactorial: it secretes proteases that degrade Clostridioides difficile toxins A and B and their intestinal receptors; it competitively inhibits adhesion and growth of enteric pathogens; it produces polyamines and short-chain fatty acids that support enterocyte trophism; it enhances secretory IgA and modulates inflammatory signaling (reducing NF-kB activation and pro-inflammatory cytokines); and it helps preserve and restore the intestinal mucosal barrier and normal microbiota disrupted by antibiotics or infection. Because it is a yeast, it is unaffected by antibacterial antibiotics.

absolute: Critically ill or severely immunocompromised patients (risk of fungemia)
Known hypersensitivity/allergy to yeast or to Saccharomyces boulardii
relative: Pregnancy and lactation (limited data; use if benefit clear)
Indwelling vascular access or recent GI surgery
Patients in close-contact care with severely immunocompromised individuals (contamination risk)
monitor: Signs of fungemia (fever, sepsis) in high-risk patients

preg: There are limited data on use during pregnancy. As a non-systemically absorbed probiotic it is generally considered to be of low risk, but it should be used during pregnancy only if the expected benefit justifies use, and avoided in immunocompromised pregnant patients.
lact: There are limited data, but as a gut-restricted probiotic it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding. Avoid handling/opening capsules around an immunocompromised infant.
renal: No dose adjustment is required; Saccharomyces boulardii acts locally in the gastrointestinal tract and is not systemically absorbed in healthy individuals.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required; it is not hepatically metabolized and acts locally in the gut.

major: Systemic antifungal agents (e.g., azoles, amphotericin, nystatin) - will kill the probiotic yeast and negate its effect; do not co-administer
moderate: MAO inhibitors - theoretical concern with tyramine in some yeast preparations (clinically minor for this product)
minor: No interaction with antibacterial antibiotics - can be co-administered intentionally
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid mixing with hot food/drinks which inactivate the yeast.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; alcohol may aggravate diarrheal symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: Can rarely be detected as Saccharomyces in blood cultures if fungemia occurs in high-risk patients.

serious: Fungemia (Saccharomyces bloodstream infection) in immunocompromised/critically ill or catheterized patients
rare: Allergic/hypersensitivity reactions to yeast (rash, urticaria, angioedema)
Fungal sepsis with seeding (e.g., endocarditis) in severely ill patients
emergency: Fungemia / fungal sepsis (fever, rigors, hypotension) in at-risk patients

monitoring: Resolution of diarrhea and stool frequency
Hydration and electrolyte status during diarrheal illness
Signs of bloodstream infection in immunocompromised or catheterized patients
counsel: This is a probiotic yeast that can be taken at the same time as your antibiotics
Do not mix it into very hot food or drinks - heat kills the live yeast
Keep drinking fluids and oral rehydration solution while you have diarrhea
Tell your doctor if you have a weakened immune system or a central line - it may not be safe for you
Stop and seek care if you develop high fever, chills, or feel very unwell
It is a supplement, not a substitute for prescribed treatment of serious infections
pk: Reaches steady gut concentration within ~3 days of regular dosing
Not systemically absorbed; acts locally in the intestinal lumen
Not applicable (cleared from gut within ~3-5 days after stopping)
Transient colonization; disappears from stool a few days after discontinuation
Store in a cool, dry place; some products require refrigeration - follow label
pearls: Yeast probiotic - intrinsically resistant to antibacterial antibiotics, so it can be given concurrently for antibiotic-associated diarrhea
Degrades C. difficile toxins A and B; useful as an adjunct (not monotherapy) for recurrent CDI
CONTRAINDICATED in critically ill, immunocompromised, or central-venous-catheter patients - rare but serious fungemia risk; avoid opening capsules near such patients
Do not co-administer with systemic antifungals, which kill it
Regulatory status: a probiotic/biotherapeutic supplement, not an FDA-approved drug - guidance from SmPC/EU products and clinical trial data
Does not permanently colonize the gut; cleared within days of stopping
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, then continue your usual schedule. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double the dose. Consistent daily use during the diarrhea or antibiotic course is what matters most.
overdose: Overdose is very unlikely to be harmful in healthy individuals; excessive intake may cause increased flatulence or bloating. There is no specific treatment beyond stopping the product and supportive care. In immunocompromised patients, any systemic infection should be treated with appropriate antifungal therapy.
